groups.title: Soft Capsule (E64600ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin E in old age, for the relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance and of stiffness of the shoulder and neck, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet at the menopause, and for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have severe renal failure; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, red patches, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability or vomiting occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamin E, peripheral circulatory disturbance, menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numb and cold hands and feet, and muscle cramps from magnesium deficiency

groups.usage: Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you are short of folic acid; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests.

Do not take it together with levodopa.

If nausea, vomiting or loose stools occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E81600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age. Through the vitamins it contains, it is used for the relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance and of stiffness of the shoulder and neck, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet at the menopause; for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain such as back pain and stiff shoulder; for the relief of dryness of the eyes, night blindness, poor development of bones and teeth, prevention of rickets, beriberi and eye fatigue. It is also used for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
If a pregnant woman takes 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day it may cause birth defects. Women who are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you are an older person; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function or kidney impairment; if you have hypoproteinaemia; if you have gout; if you have or have had kidney stones; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. If you have a tendency to thrombosis or are short of folic acid, consult a pharmacist. The vitamin A contained in this medicine is supplied sufficiently by a normal diet, so the supplementary dose must not exceed 5,000 IU a day. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a cardiac glycoside. Women taking an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen should consult a pharmacist. If you take it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene, consult a pharmacist. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, loss of appetite, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red patches, asystole, reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, pulmonary oedema or abdominal discomfort occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If menstruation comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6, C and of zinc, relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance, menopausal symptoms, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, dry eyes, night blindness, beriberi and eye fatigue, and prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and sputum.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

groups.title: Tablet (E75100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose. Ages over 7 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if the user is aged 7 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching; or if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Drowsiness may occur while taking it; avoid driving a car or operating machinery. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine. Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor used for depression or Parkinson's disease, or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Consult a pharmacist if you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs with urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, or if Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general lassitude, liver function disorder with jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E81200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have ever had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters over the whole skin or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (general lassitude, jaundice with yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.title: Soft Capsule (A20800ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin D during pregnancy and breast-feeding, during growth and in old age, and for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function or hypoproteinaemia; if you have had kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if a particular risk is expected from fat overload; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with cardiac glycosides, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat or skin rash occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Ointment (A60901COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eczema, burns, and erosion and ulceration caused by other conditions.
groups.usage: Apply it to the affected area several times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

Do not use it in the eye.

Skin irritation such as a hot feeling, itching or a stinging sensation may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (E74400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness and in old age; for the relief of pigmentation caused by sunlight or skin disease (melasma, freckles); for the prevention of bleeding gums and nosebleeds; and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gout or kidney stones; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if the user is a premature baby or a young child.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen. Taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene may cause high blood potassium, so take care. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, loss of appetite, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or pulmonary oedema occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins E, B1, B2, B6, C and of zinc, relief of pigmentation, and prevention of bleeding gums and nosebleeds

groups.title: Cream (179733CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of pain and inflammation in degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, lateral epicondylitis of the humerus (tennis elbow and the like), muscle pain, and swelling and pain after injury.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area according to symptoms, 1 to 4 times in 1 day, and rub it in gently so that it is absorbed well.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or photosensitivity; if you have had asthma caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have hypersensitivity to tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate or oxybenzone; if you are 6 months or more pregnant; or if the user is a child under 15 years of age.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have bronchial asthma, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Photosensitivity may occur, so avoid ultraviolet light while using this medicine and for up to 2 weeks after using it. Do not use it on the eyes or mucous membranes, or on athlete's foot or tinea. If it is used on damaged skin or mucous membranes, or on eczema or a rash, it may cause temporary irritation and sharp pain, so take care when using it. Do not use it under an occlusive dressing. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 week of use, stop using it and consult a pharmacist.

If, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, difficulty breathing, swelling of the face and other anaphylactoid symptoms) or an asthma attack (dry crackles, wheezing, difficulty breathing) occurs; or if, occasionally, contact dermatitis such as reddening of the skin, rash, itching, blisters, erosion, irritation or swelling, dry skin and pigmentation, photosensitivity caused by direct sunlight, or a skin rash spreading over the whole body occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis, frozen shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, tennis elbow, muscle pain, and swelling and pain after injury
